headline: Night train out of Vienna

headline: Settled with a German family in Dresden
summary: Roosevelt and Elliott move in with the Minkwitz household in Dresden, parents plus three daughters and two sons, to soak up German. Corinne lodges with another family in town, Bamie and their mother Mittie head off for spa cures, London and Paris, and Theodore Sr. stays on in Vienna before sailing home.

events.detail: Roosevelt and Elliott begin living with the Minkwitz family to learn German
Corinne boards with a different German household in Dresden
Bamie and Mittie take spa cures and visit London and Paris
Theodore Sr. remains in Vienna, then returns to America

tr_quotes.text: When we reached Dresden we younger children were left to spend the summer in the house of Herr Minckwitz, a member of either the Municipal or the Saxon Government - I have forgotten which. It was hoped that in this way we would aquire some knowledge of the German language and literature.

uncertain: Quotation is from TR's 1913 Autobiography, recalled later rather than written this day; 'aquire' kept as in source. Family name appears as both Minkwitz and Minckwitz.

headline: A schoolboy's day in Dresden
summary: Roosevelt's Dresden schedule runs from a 6:30 wake-up through nearly a full day of lessons, broken by lunch, coffee and free afternoons, until bed at ten. Anna Minkwitz drills him and Elliott in German grammar and arithmetic. Homesick Corinne moves in to join her brothers, and his collection now counts 40 animals and 220 coins.

headline: Sent to the Bastei for his health
summary: To help his health, Roosevelt is taken to the Bastei with Elliott, Corinne and the Fräuleins Anna and Emma. He hunts butterflies and reads the Nibelungenlied for the first time. Back in New York, his father watches builders at work on the family's new 57th Street house and on the natural history museum, lodging at the Union League Club meanwhile.

events.detail: Taken to the Bastei for his health with Elliott, Corinne, Anna and Emma
Collects butterflies

Theodore Sr. follows construction of the natural history museum and the new family home, staying at the Union League Club

uncertain: Source reads 'Bastel, Switzerland'; taken as the Bastei in Saxon Switzerland near Dresden, as the July 4 letter names it. Fraulein Emma's surname not given.

headline: The DLAC sits for a photograph
summary: Roosevelt, Elliott, Corinne and cousins Maud and John Elliott pose for a picture as the Dresden Literary American Club, whose motto 'W.A.N.A.' stood for 'We Are No Asses.' Corinne wrote the poems, Elliott and John the tragedies, and Roosevelt the comic tales, among them 'Mrs. Field Mouse's Dinner Party.'
